_doc: THE MIC OPENING'S SIGN — candidates (decibel PLAN 2.4; RUNNING_LOG §318; DEC-97: 'for the mic opening just like composer score, all those elements rounded corners, the 2 circles the outline and transparent fill, but can you find a highlghter yellow and let me see a few versions'). `composer`: how the composer score draws the brick today, READ from its code — the recipe to keep. `yellows`: the highlighter yellows found, each with where it comes from. `recipes`: ways of applying a yellow to a WHITE page (the composer's own recipe first). tools/signs/build_page.js draws every yellow in every recipe on score/public/signs/index.html. When he chooses, the choice becomes a row of notation/registry/rules.json (an `objects` row for the opening) by a device sheet — not this file.

composer.shape: a rectangle, corners rounded at 3 px
composer.outline: the same colour, 1.5 px, at 70 % opacity
composer.height: one fifth of the lane (never under 16 px)
composer.sign: ◉ — a dot in a ring, the two circles — then the sample's name, 11 px, dark grey #333, 6 px in from the left
composer.length: an impulse's opening is 500 ms, from 100 ms before its note; a drone's is 6 … 9 s

frame._note: the notation's video frame: 1080 px, five lanes, 12 s a page across 1848 px — so one fifth of a lane is 42 px, and 500 ms is 77 px

yellows.name: plain screen yellow
yellows.from: the convention: what most design references mean by highlighter yellow — red and green full, no blue

yellows.name: Laser Lemon
yellows.from: a Crayola fluorescent crayon colour (Wikipedia's list) — a paler, softer highlighter

yellows.name: a neon lemon
yellows.from: listed among the lemon shades on Wikipedia — a yellow leaning a little to green, as a real highlighter's ink does

yellows.name: fluorescent yellow · Electric Lime
yellows.from: the best-sourced value for fluorescent yellow (Crayola's fluorescent Electric Lime). Close to his own limeGreen #99FF00, which the score already uses for a curve

yellows.name: a Stabilo Boss yellow, as printed
yellows.from: Stabilo publishes no hex; this is one design site's reading of the pen's yellow — the ink as it looks once dry on paper, not glowing

recipes.name: exactly as the composer score
recipes.note: the fill at 35 %, the outline the same yellow at 70 %, the sign dark grey — the composer's numbers, only the colour changed

recipes.name: a denser fill
recipes.note: yellow is faint on white: the fill at 60 %, the outline nearly solid

recipes.name: the outline a shade darker
recipes.note: the fill at 45 %; the outline and the sign in the same yellow darkened by three tenths, so the brick has an edge on white paper

chosen.reads: plain yellow #FFFF00 · the fill at 35 % · the outline the same yellow, 1.5 px at 70 % · corners 3 px · the sign ◉ dark grey — the composer score's brick, the colour alone changed
